title: S3 migration of live data and the lab deploy
description:
One-time script that converts today's ~12 MB of live data into records, verified by rebuilding the old value and comparing, plus the reviewed lab deploy including the S1 bucket-policy and IAM change.
Acceptance: conversion is re-runnable and verified; cutover with workers paused; never-pay-twice and one-worker-at-a-time preserved; explicit approval from Ryan for the change set before deploy. Depends on S2a, S2b, S2c.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Starting S3: plan is Part A conversion library + CLI (runtime events, reply ledgers, job results) with write-first/commit-once protocol, dry run default, then Part B runbook and read-only production dry run.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Progress: Part A built and green locally (118 specs): record_lake_conversion.py + scripts/dev/convert_to_record_lake.py, library support (audit/convert/preview on S3RuntimeStores, S3BatchStorage, S3ConsoleStorage; check hook on commit_with_records; resume-own-owner acquire). Production dry run (read-only, get/list/head-only wrapper) succeeded: 5 journals (1 ledger, 3 runtimes, catalog), 3,817 records, control state 16,559,488 -> 1,069,869 bytes, lake +16,243,823 bytes. Next: runbook in infra/lab/README.md, docs, make check, PR.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Cutover done 2026-10-22 with Ryan's go: router HN paused (enabled=false) and worker queue mapping disabled; change set record-lake-v0-34-0 executed (v0.34.0, package 63b054b8…); conversion --apply per journal, each verified by digest/order/coverage: shared-batches 150 records (3.59 MB -> 52 KB), 3 runtimes 1,259 records each (~4.16 MB -> ~52 KB each; first runtime resumed after transient S3 timeouts, as designed), catalog 458 records (2.89 MB -> 0.99 MB). Final dry run: 5 nothing-to-convert. Queue re-enabled and router HN enabled=true at 10:52Z.
